mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, indicating supply chain disruptions, will lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle to meet demand and earnings estimates are revised downward.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 50% of months following a 1% INDPRO drop, indicating markets are shrugging off supply disruptions.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment, measured by the year-over-year change in the UNRATE series, signals a weakening labor market and slowing consumer demand that will pressure S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence (Conference Board index) rises > 5 points in the same month as the UNRATE increase, indicating labor market weakness is not denting consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) rise by more than 10% year-over-year, it signals a strong consumer demand environment that will boost S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as rising home sales and construction activity lift the broader economy.
failure_condition: 30-year mortgage rates rise > 50 basis points in the month of the HOUST increase, indicating that higher borrowing costs will dampen the housing-led growth impulse.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and rising, it signals a tightening monetary policy that will pressure S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as higher borrowing costs weigh on corporate profits and economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 60% of 60-day periods following a FEDFUNDS increase above 4%, indicating markets are shrugging off the tightening impulse.

mechanism_narrative: When real retail sales (RSAFS) decline by more than 2% month-over-month, it signals a sharp drop in consumer demand that will lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as companies cut earnings forecasts in response to the demand shock.
failure_condition: ISM manufacturing PMI rises > 2 points in the month following the RSAFS drop, indicating that the demand shock is not spilling over into the broader economy.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) rises by more than 500,000 jobs in a month, it signals a surge in labor demand that will boost consumer spending and S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as the newly employed spend their higher incomes.
failure_condition: Average hourly earnings (from PAYEMS) decline month-over-month in the same period as the job surge, indicating that the employment gains are not translating into higher consumer spending power.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% year-over-year and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2%, it signals a dangerous mix of high inflation and loose monetary policy that will lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as the Fed is forced to tighten policy aggressively to combat inflation.
failure_condition: The Fed raises rates by less than 25 basis points at the next FOMC meeting following the inflation overshoot, indicating that policymakers are not serious about fighting inflation and that the inflation scare is overblown.
